newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Business leaders hope APEC will bring more deals.
newsitem.headline: Business leaders hope APEC will bring more deals.

text.p: A group of about 50 influential Asia-Pacific business leaders meeting in Manila to advise world leaders on how to free up regional trade are hoping to go back richer by several business deals as well.
The group, called the APEC Business Advisory Council, or ABAC, has been appointed to make specific proposals to APEC leaders on improving the flow of trade and investment in the region.
Leaders of the 18-member Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) forum are due to meet in Manila on Sunday and in nearby Subic Bay the following day for their annual summit.
ABAC organisers said that apart from its advisory role, the body also hoped to be a networking mechanism that should help the business executives clinch new deals here.
"The forum provides businessmen with the venue to network with each other," ABAC chairman Roberto Romulo told Reuters on Thursday ahead of two days of ABAC meetings starting on Friday.

"It's hard to measure how much the investments and the gains of the forum will be, but they will be substantial," said Romulo, who is chairman of the Philippine Long Distance Telephone Co (PLDT), one of the largest firms in the country.
ABAC's meeting on the sidelines of the APEC summit will discuss the impact of changing trade rules on business.
APEC hopes to free up trade within the region by the year 2020 and the only complaint from the business community is that the target is too far away.
A recommendation presented by ABAC to Philippine President Fidel Ramos last month said APEC leaders should consider speeding up the implementation of APEC's goals.
In another interview recently, Romulo told Reuters that ABAC members were also concerned that the leaders did not confront politically sensitive issues.
"These are businessmen. They want action," he said.
One of the things ABAC is pushing for is China's admission to the World Trade Organisation (WTO).
Their view is that "you can't have a WTO unless you have all the major players there," Romulo said.

Specific proposals made by ABAC include the creation of an APEC business visa and APEC business immigration lanes at airports to make business-related travel easier. It also wants a series of round-table conferences in which government planners and the private sector can work to remove blocks to investment.
ABAC members are due to meet APEC leaders on November 24 to discuss their recommendations.
Heads of government due to address ABAC's meetings are President Ramos, Chile's President Eduardo Frei, Malaysian Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamad and Canadian Prime Minister Jean Chretien.
